text:
jamal: Heads up — noticed a pattern of gRPC streaming stalls across several inference pods in us-west-2 about 12:40 UTC. High p99 latencies, streams hang for ~15-30s then recover.
linh: Oof. Any packet loss/ERRs on nodes?
maria: App logs show long pauses while waiting for stream responses, retries piling up. CPU/GPU look fine.
kevin: I ran a quick tcpdump between two affected nodes: seeing lots of fragmented IPv4 packets and some out-of-order. dpkt shows DF not set on some packets.
jamal: Sounds like MTU mismatch or overlay fragmentation. Which CNI? Calico in vxlan mode (mtu 1440) on these nodes. Some ENIs are 9001 on newer instance types.
linh: That could explain it — host MTU 9001, vxlan adds 50 bytes -> pod MTU should be reduced but looks like some nodes still using 1500 for pod interfaces.
kevin: Also noticed GSO/GRO enabled on ENA NICs. When VXLAN + GSO interact badly you can get huge packets split at different layers and gRPC streaming (HTTP/2) chokes.
maria: Can we reproduce with iperf? I can spin up a server/client pair on two nodes and force large bursts.
athan: Please also check PMTU discovery state and kernel counters: ip -s link show, iptables DROP counters for fragments, and /proc/net/ipv4/ipfrag_high? Also netstat -s | grep fragment
linh: Ran these: on node-a ip link shows mtu 9001, cali+vxlan pod interface 1440, but on node-b pod iface is 1500. PMTU cache has stale entries (ip route get shows pmtu 1440 for some IPs and 1500 for others).
jamal: So mismatch across nodes — flows that transit a node with 1500 get fragmented at vxlan encapsulation and sometimes the reassembly fails leading to stalls. gRPC streams (long-lived) are sensitive to even a few lost segments.
kevin: Quick mitigation: disable GRO/GSO on host ENIs for affected nodes and set pod MTU uniformly to 1400 via a CNI config daemonset, then restart kube-proxy on those nodes. That should avoid large offloaded segments that confuse vxlan.
maria: Are we comfortable with disabling GSO on a subset of nodes? Performance hit but temporary.
jamal: It's a risk but limited window. Also can patch our calico-config to enforce MTU=1400 and roll a daemonset to set ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400 for pods created after rollout.
linh: I pushed a test DaemonSet to force MTU on the test pool and disabled GSO: `ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off` — initial tests show the gRPC stall rate dropped to near zero on the test nodes.
kevin: For longer-term: we should either standardize host MTU across instance types (9001 everywhere) or change CNI mode to ipip (smaller encaps overhead) or use/calibrate VXLAN MTU consistently. Also file a kernel BUG/ENA/vendor ticket about GSO+VXLAN interactions.
nathan: I'll open a tracking ticket with impact numbers (failed streams, retries, cost). Suggest creating an alert: if pod-level stream stalls > 5% in 5m, page oncall.
jamal: Agreed. Action items: 1) Roll MTU-fix daemonset to prod test pool (linh) 2) Temporarily disable GSO on affected nodes (kevin) 3) Create infra ticket + vendor escalation (nathan) 4) Postmortem if rollback required (maria).
sre-bot: deploy: MTU-fix-daemonset rollout started to pool=test-usw2 at 12:56 UTC.
linh: Rolling now. Will monitor traces and tcpdump for fragmentation counters.
maria: Thanks — I'll correlate application traces and push a throttled rollback plan if errors spike.
kevin: Leaving a note: when disabling GSO we saw increased CPU on network processing path but not on GPUs. Worth it short-term.
jamal: Good catch. Keep updates here, and paste tcpdump snippets if you see reassembly failures. :+1:
